author: Rebecca D. Cook
poem_text_en:
He wasn’t a hero
Known by the world,
But a hero he was
To his little girl.
My daddy was God,
Who knew all things.
And better than Santa, 
With the gifts he’d bring.
I knew his voice
Before I could speak.
And loves it when
He would sing me to sleep.
He taught me life’s lessons
Or right from wrong
And instilled in me values
That I might be strong.
And so, dear Dad
My best memory to recall
Is the gift of your presence,
The greatest gift of all.
summary_en: The poem reflects a daughter's heartfelt tribute to her father, who was not famous to the world but a hero in her eyes. It emphasizes that his presence, love, and moral guidance were the most precious gifts she received throughout her childhood. The poet highlights the father's role as a teacher, protector, and a source of security.

glossary.meaning_en: Gradually established something (such as an idea or attitude) in a person's mind.
The state or fact of being present or existing in a place.

figures_of_speech.note_en: The poet compares the father to God to signify his omnipotence and importance in her life.
Repetition of the 'r' sound in close proximity.

rules.rule_en: Theme: The deep emotional bond between a daughter and her father.
The father is described as better than Santa Claus because of the gifts he brought, which were symbolic of his love and presence.
